if C2 arrives first: B accepts Ok("-SECOND"), then C1 -> The message key with the given key can't be created, message index: 1 [MissingMessageKey(1)]
so which of two authentic messages is delivered depends on arrival order; the sender cannot tell

converse hazard: if the ratchet state is persisted but the process dies before the plaintext is stored/acked, redelivery of the ciphertext is rejected (the message key is gone) and the message content is lost; ratchet state and the received message must be committed in ONE atomic transaction

RULE (sender): encrypt -> persist session pickle (fsync/atomic rename) -> only then release ciphertext to the transport. RULE (receiver): decrypt -> in one atomic commit persist {new session pickle, plaintext/inbox record, dedupe id} -> only then ack. Violation costs: send side = lost message + AES key/IV reuse; receive side = duplicate delivery (rollback) or permanent message loss (state ahead of data).
